    • instantiate

      protected Seq instantiate(ClassLoader envLoader)
      A generator that asks for a native sequence cannot be configured on a database that has no sequence objects: NativeJDBCSeq needs DBDictionary.nextSequenceQuery, and refuses to configure without it. Jakarta Persistence leaves the realisation of a generator to the provider, so rather than fail, such a generator is backed by a ValueTableJDBCSeq - a counter row keyed by the sequence name, which keeps the identifiers unique and honours initialValue and allocationSize.

      The substitution happens here, where the sequence is resolved, so the runtime and the mapping tool agree on which sequence backs the generator, and it produces a separate metadata instance rather than mutating this one, which is shared.

      Overrides:
      instantiate in class SequenceMetaData
      See Also:
      • Compatibility.getEmulateNativeSequences()
